extracted.intended_audience: educators, artists, engineers, and general readers interested in developing mental imagery and memory
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for training and evaluating the 'visualizing' faculty (mental imagery and sight-memory) for learners and practitioners (artists, engineers, workmen). Covers desired capacities, pedagogical methods, and practical applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call_up_clear_steady_complete_mental_image
rubrics_metrics.description: The capacity of calling up at will a clear, steady, and complete mental image of any object that we have recently examined and studied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the primary aim: be able to summon a detailed image on demand. The author adds that one should be able to project any of its images on paper and draw its outline there (see related pedagogical exercises). Examples: pupils trained by Lecoq de Boisbaudran could summon images at will, hold them steady, and draw them with fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualize_object_from_any_aspect_and_embrace_all_sides
rubrics_metrics.description: We should be able to visualize that object freely from any aspect; we should be able to embrace all sides of the object simultaneously in a single perception, or at least to sweep all sides successively with so rapid a mental glance as to arrive at practically the same result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should develop the ability to rotate, reverse, or shift mental images (e.g., reverse left-right as in a mirror). Examples include imagining all sides of a crystal or visualizing a person on a mental stage. This capacity allows constructing a generic, scale-correct image from many observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project_image_on_paper_and_draw_outline
rubrics_metrics.description: We should be able to project any of [an object's] images on paper and draw its outline there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A teachable skill: learners can practice holding a mental picture on an imagined sheet and tracing it. The author cites exercises where pupils follow outlines at a distance with a pencil to link sight-memory with muscular memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct_and_alter_images_from_description
rubrics_metrics.description: We ought to be able to construct images from description or otherwise, and to alter them in whatever way we please.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This emphasizes imagination and manipulation of mental images (building, adding, subtracting, altering). Important for thinking, problem solving, and creating generalized images from varying inputs (e.g., forming a generic 'four-oar' from many sightings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine_similar_images_into_single_generic_image
rubrics_metrics.description: We ought to acquire the power of combining separate, but more or less similar, images into a single generic one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author reports experiments (optical superposition, composite photography) showing generalized portraits form when component images share moderate resemblance, same point of view and size. Pedagogically, training should encourage creating generalized, prototypical images rather than over-specific instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carry_away_snapshots_of_complex_scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: We should learn to carry away pictures at a glance of a more complicated scene than we can succeed at the moment in analyzing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a retinal/brief-flash memory so that a rapidly-seen scene persists and can be studied afterward. Useful for analyzing details that escaped initial observation; practice can strengthen this 'retentive' faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquire_memories_based_on_thorough_understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: The memories we should aim at acquiring are chiefly such as are based on a thorough understanding of the objects observed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority should be given to understanding what is observed (logical associations, structural comprehension) rather than rote visual recall. The healthiest memory multiplies logical associations and uses several senses in due proportion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical_drawing_memory_exactness
rubrics_metrics.description: In the processes of mechanical drawing, the intended structure has to be portrayed so exactly in plan, elevation, side view, and sections that the workman has simply to copy the drawing in metal, wood, or stone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For mechanicians, engineers and architects, visual memory must support exact multi-view representations. Training should aim for precision in multiple projections so that the drawing unambiguously specifies fabrication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen_memory_by_multiplying_logical_associations
rubrics_metrics.description: The art of strengthening visual as well as every other form of memory lies in multiplying associations; the healthiest memory being that in which all the associations are logical, and toward which all the senses concur in their due proportions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multi-sensory and logically connected cues to build durable memories. The author notes that vividness increases when two or more lines of association are simultaneously excited. Avoid isolated or non-logical associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical_method_study_models_then_draw_from_memory
rubrics_metrics.description: A favored expedient: pupils were made to study the models thoroughly before they tried to draw them from memory; associate sight-memory with muscular memory by making pupils follow at a distance the outlines of the figures with a pencil held in their hands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence (Lecoq de Boisbaudran) shows that systematic practice—studying models, then reproducing from memory while linking hand motions—greatly strengthens visual memory and drawing fidelity. After months of practice pupils could summon, hold, and draw mental images reliably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain_retinal_picture_after_brief_exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: A useful faculty, easily developed by practice, is that of retaining a mere retinal picture: a scene is flashed upon the eye; the memory of it persists, and details which escaped observation during the brief time when it was actually seen may be analyzed and studied at leisure in the subsequent vision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice brief-exposure observation and immediate analysis to capture fleeting details. This skill is valuable for rapid assessment and later study of complex scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot_force_recall_by_will_positive_method
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a mistake to suppose that a powerful exercise of the will can vivify a faint image. The action of the will is negative, being limited to the suppression of what is not wanted and would be in the way. It cannot create thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When unable to recall (e.g., a forgotten name), the recommended technique is to stop forcing recall and think of other things until a chance association suggests the missing item. Avoid over-concentration; refresh the mind by changing scene or occupation to restore discursiveness and idea flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualize_before_action_in_handicrafts_and_professions
rubrics_metrics.description: Workmen ought to visualize the whole of what they propose to do before they take a tool in their hands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For smiths, carpenters, mechanicians, engineers, architects, dressmakers, decorators, strategists, artists and experimentalists: visualize the intended operation comprehensively to give accuracy to perception and justness to generalizations. Education should cultivate this habit rather than starve it.
